necessary_context.content: Euclidean x in R^d1, y in R^d2; f continuously differentiable. Assumption 1 bounds each partial-gradient difference by ell(||x1-x2||+||y1-y2||). Assumption 2 requires a saddle point and attained blockwise extrema with finite values. Definition 2 requires uniform mu1,mu2>0 and ||grad_x f(x,y)||^2>=2mu1[f(x,y)-min_u f(u,y)], ||grad_y f(x,y)||^2>=2mu2[max_v f(x,v)-f(x,y)] for every x,y.
necessary_context.name: Standing model and two-sided PL

necessary_context.content: Assumption 3: unbiased partial-gradient estimators with variance bounded by sigma^2>0. Algorithm 1 draws two i.i.d. samples per iteration. g(x)=max_y f(x,y), g*=min_x g(x), a_t=E[g(x_t)-g*], b_t=E[g(x_t)-f(x_t,y_t)], P_t=a_t+b_t/10. Page 5 defines L=ell+ell^2/mu2; its smoothness proof, attributed to [47], was not read.
